_about: AI-GENERATED (Claude Opus 5.5, 2026-11-15), NOT YET REVIEWED BY A HUMAN. The L2 plan (concepts/Layout/L2/layouts.json) as built on the kit's 2 m grid: the wall runs KitOfficeScene.cs places and make_markings.py marks, so the marks stop exactly at the built doorways. Plan metres, x east and y south from the NW corner. 'half' is firm A's half; the builder also places it turned 180 degrees about (20, 16) for firm B. A run's thickness lies on the right of its direction of travel as the plan is drawn (east -> south side). doors: 'at' is the door's centre on the run's axis; 'room' names the room behind it (rooms below) and 'face' points from the wall to the corridor side its plate faces; a door without a room gets no plate. trimA / trimB: metres off a run's start or end where it meets the facade (0.15 curtain wall, 0.2 window sill), so it stops at the glass. The ground-floor wall under E1's upper flight sits south of y 14 and the stair hole starts at x 11.8, so neither cuts the flight. Glass kinds (mood D, 2026-11-15): fluted = full-height reeded frost (back rooms), louvre = frosted slats with see-through gaps (rooms lit in their half's blue), frost = fluted bands with clear glass at eye height, glass = clear. Snaps from layouts.json: doors move to odd metres (2 m door pieces); the back office's ring door moves from y 24 to 21 and its north door from x 2 to 1; the feature flight's top moves from x 16.4 to 16.

districts._about: Firm A's half; turned for firm B (L -> R, A -> C). H is the shared court strip between the cores. Bounded by walls: x 14 is E1's east wall line, y 16 the legal conference's south wall line.

built._about: Where the build departs from layouts.json's geometry: the upper slab's void and holes on the 2 m grid, the feature flight, the lift door.

decals._about: Wall decals, firm A's half, both floors unless 'floor' says. at: plan point on the wall face; face: the direction the decal faces; y: centre height, metres.
decals._wallTextAbout: Wall text (posters/COPY.md 'Wall text', Alex 2026-11-15): each run is wall faces in reading order; each face carries one whole message of its own (Alex: 'one per wall, the wrapping is confusing'). a -> b along the face as the reader reads it (left to right), face = the direction it faces, ink = its colour (white over the cobalt fields, navy on white). Firm A's half; turned for B. Centre height and letter height in KitOfficeScene.
